artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan (5.5h) to prune dot-prefixed directories from literature-build-index.sh manifest discovery, add warn-by-default duplicate-doc_id detection with a --strict-duplicates fatal mode, report database-derived per-doc_id counts, lock it in with a scratch-dir regression test, document the shared corpus-directory predicate, and eliminate the manual chunks.json.bak workaround with a verified live rebuild.

memory_candidates.content: In ~/Projects/Literature/, dot-prefixed directories appear at BOTH the corpus root (.backups, .sources-recovered, .online-ingest-staging, .memory, .git, .claude) and nested inside a document directory (sources/thomas_2003_reactive/.chunks/ holds two superseded per-chapter chunks.json manifests). A traversal-safety prune for the corpus must therefore exclude dot-prefixed directories at ANY depth, not just at the root, and must use `find "$dir" -mindepth 1 \( -name '.*' -type d -prune \) -o \( -name 'chunks.json' -print \)` so that explicitly targeting a dot-named directory (--dir .../.backups) does not self-prune. Verified: 206 manifests bare, 204 pruned, zero doc_ids lost.
